claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the children you're claiming for. 

**What is the age of the child (or children) you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

Please provide their current age(s), and I'll guide you through the eligibility requirements based on their age group.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm inquiring about my child Alex. He's 19 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about **Alex, who is 19 years old** and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 19 years old (in the 16-19 age range), I need to check some additional criteria. Let me get more details about Alex's situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
For a 19-year-old, Child Benefit eligibility depends on their education or training status. I need to ask you about **Alex's current situation**:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In education or training** (e.g., attending school, college, university, or an approved training course)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the past 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and not recently left education?

Please let me know which applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in education. He's studying for his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So **Alex is currently in education, studying for A-levels at college**. This is very relevant to the eligibility assessment.

Let me check the specific education requirements for 16-19 year olds:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I can see that A-levels are an approved education qualification. Now I need to clarify a few more details about Alex's education to ensure it meets the full criteria:

**Question 1:** Is Alex studying **A-levels on a full-time basis** with at least **12 hours per week of supervised study**?

**Question 2:** Is Alex **married**? (If he is, I'll need to check if he's financially dependent on you, as this affects eligibility)

Please let me know the answers to these questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is studying full-time at college - definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! So **Alex is studying A-levels full-time with more than 12 hours per week of supervised study, and is not married**. This is excellent news for eligibility.

Now let me navigate through the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Since Alex is in approved education, this is the next check we need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does work quite a bit actually. He has a part-time job at the supermarket, and it's pretty much full-time hours - he works more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. So **Alex is working more than 24 hours per week** at his supermarket job, while also studying A-levels full-time.

Unfortunately, this affects his Child Benefit eligibility. Let me navigate to confirm the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the eligibility criteria, I'm afraid I have some disappointing news:

---

## **INELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**Reason:** Child aged 16+ is working 24 or more hours per week

**Why this matters for Alex:**
While Alex qualifies in many respects (he's 19, in approved education studying A-levels full-time, and lives with you), the rule states that children aged 16+ who work **24 or more hours per week** cannot receive Child Benefit.

Even though Alex is in approved education, the 24+ hours per week work rule applies to those aged 16 and over.

**What this means:**
- Child Benefit cannot be paid for Alex while he continues to work these hours
- **However**, if Alex's work hours were to reduce to less than 24 hours per week, you could potentially claim Child Benefit again
- Or, if Alex stops working altogether (while remaining in full-time approved education), you would be eligible to claim

**Next steps:**
- If Alex's work situation changes in the future, you may wish to reapply
- You can contact HMRC for further advice or to discuss your specific circumstances

I'm sorry this isn't a positive outcome. Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. Just to be clear though - so even though he's in full-time education doing his A-levels, because he's working more than 24 hours a week, that means I can't get Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. I understand it's disappointing!

To summarize the situation with **Alex**:

**What qualifies him:**
✓ He's 19 years old (within the eligible age range)
✓ He's in full-time, approved education (A-levels at college)
✓ He's studying more than 12 hours per week
✓ He's not married
✓ He lives with you

**What disqualifies him:**
✗ He's working **more than 24 hours per week**

The rule is clear: **Children aged 16+ who work 24 or more hours per week are not eligible for Child Benefit**, even if they're simultaneously in full-time approved education.

The rationale is that at 16+, if someone is working substantial hours (24+), they're expected to have enough income that Child Benefit isn't necessary.

**The good news:** If Alex's circumstances change—for example, if he reduces his work hours to less than 24 per week—you could potentially reapply for Child Benefit at that point.

For now though, unfortunately you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Is there anything else I can help you with, or did you want to check eligibility for any other children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child. Thank you for explaining it all clearly - I understand now. It's a shame, but at least I know where I stand. I appreciate your help.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you, even though it's not the outcome you were hoping for.

Let me provide you with the formal eligibility determination:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary of your eligibility assessment:**

**For Alex (age 19):** **NOT ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit

**Reason:** Working 24+ hours per week disqualifies him, despite being in full-time approved education.

If you have any questions in the future or if Alex's circumstances change (particularly if his work hours reduce), feel free to reach out or contact HMRC directly for advice.

Thank you for using this service, and best of luck with everything!
